prior_results_known: TASK-0004 source and target performance and the illustrative fraction calculation were already inspected before this design.
question: How does constituent PID affect quark-fraction inference bias and uncertainty when transferring a Pythia-trained classifier to Herwig?
estimand: Quark probability f of the IID mixture generating process. Realized class counts fluctuate binomially.
response: Pythia class-conditional acceptance at each checkpoint's original strict frozen cut.
boundaries: Keep point estimates and diagnostic intervals unbounded. Report out-of-range rates. No silent clipping or seed ensembling.
source_partition: Split the existing Pythia final-test rows 50/50 within each class into response and pseudo-data pools using one seeded permutation. Persist row IDs and reuse the partition across all models and seeds.
pseudo_data: For each replicate draw K~Binomial(N,f), then sample K quark rows and N-K gluon rows with replacement. Share those rows across all model and seed columns. Independent child stream per fraction/sample-size cell, ordered fraction first.
task0006_checks: Algebraic closure plus disjoint-pool Pythia pseudoexperiments. Compare each Monte Carlo mean with the analytic expectation conditional on both observed pools. A discrepancy exceeding 5 Monte Carlo standard errors flags a numerical diagnostic. Source-pool uncertainty and coverage are evaluated in TASK-0007.
primary_followup_contrast: PFN-ID minus PFN-K in absolute inference bias on Herwig, averaging per-seed absolute biases. Negative means less bias with PID.
task0007_uncertainty: Propagate pseudo-data binomial uncertainty and independent source-response binomial uncertainty at fixed models and numerical cuts. Verify nominal coverage with repeated source-response and pseudo-data samples before interpreting target coverage. Resampling is paired across model/seed columns. Training-seed variation is reported separately. Threshold-selection and retraining uncertainty remain outside this protocol.
